# Profile

My background spans scientific modelling, software development, data science, and machine learning. I am particularly interested in systems whose behaviour can be evaluated, whose outputs can be traced to evidence, and whose implementation remains maintainable.

## Technical focus

- Software engineering, Python development, testing, and maintainability
- Data analysis, statistical reasoning, and machine learning
- Model evaluation, error analysis, and benchmark design
- Large language models and source-grounded knowledge systems
- Applied mathematics, numerical simulation, and environmental modelling

These areas represent different kinds of experience and ongoing work; they should not be interpreted as equivalent levels of expertise. The [Skills](skills.qmd) page connects claims to concrete examples where possible.

## Selected scientific work

My earlier scientific work includes publications on reduced-order modelling and environmental dispersion:

- [Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion (2008)](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14)
- [Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite (2006)](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/)

## Approach

I aim to make technical work understandable through clear problem statements, justified design choices, appropriate tests and evaluation protocols, and explicit limitations.
